risks.description: Excessive rainfall may cause waterlogging in transplanted fields
High humidity promotes bacterial leaf blight
Temperatures within acceptable range for transplanting

High.recommendation: Heavy rainfall is expected during the next 24–48 hours. Delay transplanting until rainfall subsides. Ensure field drainage channels are clear. If transplanting has already begun, monitor for seedling mortality and prepare for gap filling.

risks.description: Moderate rainfall may temporarily waterlog low-lying areas

Moderate.recommendation: Moderate rainfall expected. Transplanting can proceed in well-drained fields. Avoid transplanting in low-lying areas for the next 24 hours. Maintain 2–3 cm standing water in the field after transplanting.

Low.recommendation: Weather conditions are favorable for transplanting. Proceed with planned operations. Ensure adequate irrigation is available if rainfall is insufficient.

risks.description: High temperatures may cause spikelet sterility

High.recommendation: Critical flowering stage — heavy rain and high humidity expected. Apply fungicide spray for blast disease prevention if not already done. Avoid applying nitrogen fertilizer during this period. Monitor panicles for damage after heavy rainfall.

risks.description: Moderate rainfall, panicles should not be affected
Monitor for early signs of blast

Moderate.recommendation: Conditions are generally favorable for flowering. Monitor fields regularly for signs of blast or sheath blight. Maintain recommended water levels in the field. Apply need-based plant protection measures.

Low.recommendation: Weather conditions are favorable for the flowering stage. Continue routine crop management. Ensure adequate water supply for grain formation.

risks.description: Heavy rainfall will damage flowers and reduce fruit set
Wet conditions promote late blight and bacterial wilt
Temperatures are within range for tomato

High.recommendation: Heavy rainfall is expected during the next 24 hours. Avoid unnecessary irrigation and monitor the field for waterlogging. Apply mulch around plants to prevent soil splashing. Spray copper-based fungicide as a preventive measure for late blight. Ensure adequate drainage in the field.

Moderate.recommendation: Moderate rainfall expected. Ensure field drainage is clear. Monitor plants for early signs of blight or wilting. Staking and mulching will help keep fruits off wet soil. Schedule spraying operations for dry periods between rain spells.

risks.description: Light rain, beneficial for the crop

Low.recommendation: Weather conditions are favorable for flowering. Continue regular irrigation and nutrient management. This is a good window for applying foliar micronutrients to support fruit set.

risks.description: Heavy rainfall may cause fruit cracking and rot
Wet and humid conditions promote fruit rot
High temperatures may affect fruit quality

High.recommendation: Significant rainfall is expected. Harvest any mature and nearly-mature fruits immediately to prevent rain damage and fruit cracking. Ensure support structures (staking) are secure. Apply post-rain fungicide spray if conditions allow. Prioritize drainage management.

risks.description: Moderate rain may cause some fruit issues

Moderate.recommendation: Moderate rainfall expected. Monitor fruits for cracking. Harvest ripe fruits promptly. Maintain good air circulation around plants by pruning lower leaves. Apply preventive fungicide if needed.

Low.recommendation: Conditions are favorable for fruit development. Continue regular irrigation schedule. Apply potassium-rich fertilizer to improve fruit quality and shelf life. Harvest at appropriate maturity.

risks.description: Soybean is sensitive to waterlogging during flowering

High.recommendation: Heavy rainfall expected. Soybean flowering is highly sensitive to waterlogging. Ensure field drainage is functional. Avoid any field operations during wet conditions. Monitor for soybean rust symptoms (pustules on lower leaves) after the rain spell.

risks.description: Some waterlogging risk in low-lying patches

Moderate.recommendation: Moderate rainfall expected. Ensure inter-row drainage. If preventive rust spray has not been applied, consider scheduling it for the next dry window. Monitor plant health and pest activity.

Low.recommendation: Conditions are favorable for soybean flowering. This is a good time for routine scouting and weed management. Ensure adequate moisture is available during this critical reproductive stage.

risks.description: Temperatures are above optimal for wheat heading
Current season rainfall is not expected to affect wheat
Warm humid conditions may promote rust

Moderate.recommendation: Temperatures are above optimal for wheat heading. If possible, apply a light irrigation during cooler parts of the day to moderate canopy temperature. Monitor for yellow or brown rust symptoms. Avoid nitrogen application at this stage.

Low.recommendation: Favorable conditions for wheat heading. Continue regular monitoring. Ensure adequate soil moisture for grain development. No immediate action required.
